newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG parliament rejects censure motion against Chan.
newsitem.headline: PNG parliament rejects censure motion against Chan.

text.p: The parliament of Papua New Guinea on Tuesday rejected a motion calling on Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan to stand aside, giving him unexpected respite after a week of political crisis over a mercenary deal.

Members of parliament voted by 58 to 39 against the motion, introduced by opposition parties, which called on Chan, Deputy Prime Minister Chris Haiveta and Defence Minister Mathias Ijape to stand aside while an inquiry was held into the contract to use mercenaries against an uprising on Bougainville island.
The vote was taken after nearly five hours of rowdy debate, during which Chan took the floor only once to defend his mercenary plans on grounds of national security.

"Sometimes you have to make decisions in the best interests of the security of the nation and we made this decision and will not compromise that decision," Chan told the parliament. "I had to put the lives of our soldiers on Bougainville first."
The vote represents a victory for Chan after a week of setbacks. It was unclear, however, how it would go down with rebel military officers who have repeatedly demanded his resignation.
